newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's rice stocks to grow further -- farm ministry.
newsitem.headline: Japan's rice stocks to grow further -- farm ministry.

text.p: The Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday that Japan's domestic rice stocks are expected to rise to 3.1 million tonnes as of the end of October due to good harvests in the past three years.
This compares with 2.94 million tonnes in October of last year, the ministry said. Good harvests in the past three years have swollen stocks in grain warehouses across the country.
The ministry said Japan's rice supplies for this calendar year are expected to reach 13.77 million tonnes, including imported rice, while demand is expected to total nearly 10.80 million tonnes.
"Given the carry-over stocks from the previous year, domestic rice stocks are expected to grow further," the ministry said in a report.
The report also said rice stocks at the end of October 1998 are expected to have fallen to between 2.80 and 2.90 million tonnes.
Japan's annual rice consumption has fallen steadily from 13.41 million tonnes in 1963 to 10.49 million tonnes in 1995, the ministry said.
The ministry's report said that constant set-aside of rice planting is needed for a balanced supply/demand situation in Japan.

On Japan's rice import policy, the ministry said in the report it would buy a certain amount of foreign rice under GATT agreements, particularly new crops. But the report did not give a detailed schedule for rice import tenders this year.
Japan opened its long-closed rice market in 1993 under the GATT agreement. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
